React Integration

Updated October 9, 2026
文AAlso available in:Deutsch,Español,Français,Italiano,日本語

Connect your React or Next.js application to MyFormCapture using a clean, reusable component. Manage local form state, submit data asynchronously via fetch, and show instant loading and success confirmation feedback to your users.

What you’ll build

Section titled “What you’ll build”

In this guide, you will build a clean React form component (ContactForm.jsx) with:

  • Controlled state for name, email, and message fields.
  • Submission handling via asynchronous fetch POST.
  • Loading indicator while the request is in flight.
  • Success confirmation message without triggering a full page reload.

Project folder structure

Section titled “Project folder structure”

Structure your React project components as follows:

React Project Structure
src/
├── components/
│ └── ContactForm.jsx     ← Reusable form component
├── App.jsx                 ← Imports and renders ContactForm
└── main.jsx                ← React root mounting point

The ContactForm.jsx component

Section titled “The ContactForm.jsx component”

Create a new file at src/components/ContactForm.jsx and add the following code:

src/components/ContactForm.jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';

export default function ContactForm() {
const [formData, setFormData] = useState({
  name: '',
  email: '',
  message: ''
});

const [status, setStatus] = useState('idle'); // 'idle' | 'submitting' | 'success' | 'error'

const handleChange = (e) => {
  setFormData({
    ...formData,
    [e.target.name]: e.target.value
  });
};

const handleSubmit = async (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  setStatus('submitting');

  try {
    // Replace 'demo-form-uuid' with your genuine MyFormCapture endpoint
    const response = await fetch('https://myformcapture.com/f/demo-form-uuid', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(formData)
    });

    if (response.ok) {
      setStatus('success');
      setFormData({ name: '', email: '', message: '' });
    } else {
      setStatus('error');
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Submission failed:', err);
    setStatus('error');
  }
};

if (status === 'success') {
  return (
    <div className="alert-success">
      <h3>Thank you!</h3>
      <p>Your message has been sent successfully. We will be in touch soon.</p>
      <button onClick={() => setStatus('idle')}>Send another message</button>
    </div>
  );
}

return (
  <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="contact-form">
    <div className="form-group">
      <label htmlFor="name">Your Name</label>
      <input
        type="text"
        id="name"
        name="name"
        value={formData.name}
        onChange={handleChange}
        placeholder="Sam Smith"
        required
      />
    </div>

    <div className="form-group">
      <label htmlFor="email">Email Address</label>
      <input
        type="email"
        id="email"
        name="email"
        value={formData.email}
        onChange={handleChange}
        placeholder="sam@example.com"
        required
      />
    </div>

    <div className="form-group">
      <label htmlFor="message">Message</label>
      <textarea
        id="message"
        name="message"
        value={formData.message}
        onChange={handleChange}
        rows="4"
        placeholder="Tell us about your project..."
        required
      />
    </div>

    {status === 'error' && (
      <p className="error-text">Something went wrong. Please try again.</p>
    )}

    <button type="submit" disabled={status === 'submitting'}>
      {status === 'submitting' ? 'Submitting...' : 'Send Message'}
    </button>
  </form>
);
}

Importing into App.jsx

Section titled “Importing into App.jsx”

Import and render your newly created ContactForm component inside App.jsx:

src/App.jsx
import React from 'react';
import ContactForm from './components/ContactForm';

export default function App() {
return (
  <div className="app-container">
    <header className="page-header">
      <h1>Get in Touch</h1>
      <p>Have questions? Reach out to our team.</p>
    </header>

    <main className="form-wrapper">
      <ContactForm />
    </main>
  </div>
);
}

Component architecture breakdown

Section titled “Component architecture breakdown”
1

Controlled Input State

We use React’s standard useState hook to bind form values, guaranteeing synchronized field state across user typing.

2

Asynchronous POST Request

The fetch request sends JSON data with Accept: application/json header. MyFormCapture responds with a JSON confirmation status code (HTTP 200), preventing page reload.

3

Interactive UI States

The status state toggles between idle, submitting, and success to provide immediate visual feedback.

Illustrative Integration Example This React example is illustrative. The endpoint https://myformcapture.com/f/demo-form-uuid serves as a placeholder. In your live deployment, provide your active form endpoint from your MyFormCapture administration panel.
